title: How Notable Capital, GIC, and Baillie Gifford bet big on Anthropic before its IPO
lede: Notable Capital, GIC and Baillie Gifford explain to TechCrunch what convinced them to put billions into Anthropic at valuations that once looked extreme, ahead of its record IPO.

points: Notable put about 10% of the US part of its $1 billion-plus fund into the Series E at $61.5 billion, after finding developers chose Claude over ChatGPT 70% of the time.
Anthropic raised $81.3 billion in its IPO at a fully diluted valuation near $1.5 trillion, about a 15x paper return for Notable.
GIC first came in at the $183 billion Series F, then co-led the Series G at $380 billion and the pre-IPO round at $965 billion.
Across those rounds GIC invested more than $4.5 billion, for roughly 1% of the company after the IPO, according to a person familiar.
Baillie Gifford put in $1.5 billion over three rounds, citing consistent execution, revenue and gross margins.

sections.text: Two of the three backers name developer adoption, Claude's share of developer usage and early Claude Code traction, as the signal behind their bet.
